subject: POC trial - environment selection and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeai.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmeai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial - environment selection and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment across teams. Below is a short recap, proposed success criteria, and recommended next steps so we can lock down the trial environment. I attached a one-page POC plan and a network diagram for the VPC option.

Recap (what we agreed):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme AI's chat assistant use case (live user-facing inference).
- Primary metrics: latency, throughput, and cost per 1k requests.
- Security: data residency + KMS for encryption at rest are required.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency under 220ms for 512-token requests (95% of test cases).
2) Throughput: sustain 15k–25k inference reqs/day during test window with autoscaling behavior.
3) Quality: model outputs meet your scoring rubric (intent accuracy >= 92% on the evaluation set).
4) Cost target: unit cost <= $0.003/token (target for evaluation only).

Evaluation plan & timeline (3 weeks recommended):
- Week 0 (this week): environment selection + sign-off (hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC).
- Week 1: baseline tests (hosted or sandbox) + initial eval set runs; SE config and prefix caching enabled.
- Week 2: load tests, failover, and latency tuning; integrate KMS and logging for audit sample.
- Week 3: final validation, handoff to ops with runbook.

Environment options (tradeoffs):
- Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-managed, quickest to start, limited network config; good for initial quality and latency tests.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity): predictable performance, better isolation for consistent latency testing; requires capacity commit and a short provisioning window (typically 3–5 business days).
- VPC trial (private): customer VPC peering or private endpoints, supports your KMS and strict network controls; longer setup (network config + security approvals) but meets your compliance needs.

Recommendation: start with a hosted trial for immediate quality checks while we parallelize VPC setup. If performance variability becomes a blocker, we standby to provision a dedicated sandbox for week 2.

Ownership & asks:
- Jordan / Sam: confirm which environment you want to kick off first (hosted or VPC). If VPC, please share the network contact + preferred CIDR and the team that will provision the peering/firewall rules.
- Neha (SE): will own test harness, model variant selection, and run the baseline benchmarks.
- Vivek (solutions): will coordinate security questionnaire / SOC 2 evidence if needed.

Next steps (please reply with items below):
1) Pick environment for Week 0 (hosted preferred for speed).
2) If VPC: provide internal network contact, CIDR + egress rules, allowed IPs, and KMS key ARN.
3) Share evaluation dataset (or sample) and scoring rubric by EOD Friday.
4) Schedule a 60-min setup call with Neha and infra (propose Wed or Thu next week).

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC checklist), network_diagram.png (VPC topology).

Thanks — I'll stand up a calendar invite once you confirm the environment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial - environment selection and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. Quick questions:  
1) For the dedicated sandbox option, what hardware / instance profile do you recommend for a 15k–25k req/day target and the latency goals? Do you have a ballpark cost estimate for a 2-week sandbox?
2) For the VPC trial, is there support for customer-managed KMS and SAML-based access? We'll need both for our compliance team sign-off.

We like the idea of starting hosted to validate quality, but if the dedicated sandbox can be spun up quickly and cost-effectively we may prefer that to avoid noisy neighbors impacting latency.

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial - environment selection and next steps

Jordan — good questions, answered inline below.

Dedicated sandbox (recommended sizing for your workload):
- Typical test config we recommend: 1 x A10G or equivalent (good price/perf) for baseline; for tighter latency targets 1 x A100 / A500 (higher perf).
- For 15k–25k req/day and p95 ~220ms at 512 tokens, 1 x A10G dedicated with optimized batching and KV cache should be sufficient for the evaluation set.
- Ballpark cost (Redwood pricing example): a 2-week dedicated sandbox on A10G ~ $6k–$9k depending on sustained hours and storage (we'll provide a precise quote once you pick instance type & hours).

VPC trial support: 
- Yes — we support customer-managed KMS (provide key ARN) and SAML for user provisioning. For the VPC option we'll need:
  * CIDR blocks for peering or list of allowed outbound IPs
  * Security contact email and a dedicated point-of-contact to approve firewall rules
  * Expected duration of the trial (helps us pre-provision logs/retention)

Plan to run hosted baseline in parallel:
- Neha will spin up a hosted trial within 48 hours to run the initial quality checks while we set up VPC networking in parallel. That keeps momentum and gives you quick results.

Next steps (updated):
1) Jordan/Sam: confirm preference to start hosted + parallel VPC setup OR to move directly to a dedicated sandbox.
2) If going VPC: please share CIDR, egress rules, and KMS ARN by EOD Thursday so infra can begin the peering runbook.
3) I'll get you a dedicated sandbox quote within 24 hours if you want to compare numbers.

I attached a rough network diagram showing our recommended VPC peering and minimal firewall rules.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks — we had an internal sync and want to go ahead with the VPC trial (customer-managed KMS + SAML). A few quick confirmations and asks:

1) VPC timeline: can your team complete the peering and initial validation by next Tuesday (23 Jun)? We can prioritize infra to get you CIDR and the firewall ticket today.
2) Required firewall rules / IPs: please provide a short list of outbound IPs or CIDR ranges we need to allow (or confirm if peering is preferred).
3) Contact for infra onboarding: please loop in our infra lead, Maya Rao (maya.rao@acmeai.com) — she will own the firewall change and peering configuration.

Action items from our side:
- I'll open a firewall ticket and share the ticket number once created.
- We'll send the KMS key ARN and SAML metadata by EOD today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Once we have the peering details I suggest a 60-min onboarding call with Neha and Maya on Mon/Tue next week.
